# Characterization of Pointwise Minimum of Real-Valued Functions

## Theorem
Let $S$ be a set.
Let $\mathbb{R}$ denote the real number line.
Let $f, g: S \to \mathbb{R}$ be real-valued functions.
Let $f \wedge g$ denote the pointwise minimum of $f$ and $g$, defined as $(f \wedge g)(s) = \min\{f(s), g(s)\}$ for all $s \in S$.
Then $f \wedge g = \frac{1}{2}(f + g - |f - g|)$.

## Proof
Let $s \in S$ be an arbitrary element of the domain. We evaluate both sides of the equation at $s$.
By definition of the pointwise minimum, the left hand side evaluated at $s$ is:
$$(f \wedge g)(s) = \min\{f(s), g(s)\}.$$

By definition of pointwise operations, the right hand side evaluated at $s$ is:
$$\frac{1}{2}\left(f(s) + g(s) - |f(s) - g(s)|\right).$$

We consider two mutually exclusive cases:

**Case 1:** $f(s) \le g(s)$
In this case, $\min\{f(s), g(s)\} = f(s)$.
Since $f(s) \le g(s)$, we have $f(s) - g(s) \le 0$, which implies $|f(s) - g(s)| = -(f(s) - g(s)) = g(s) - f(s)$.
Substituting this into the right hand side expression, we get:
$$\frac{1}{2}\left(f(s) + g(s) - (g(s) - f(s))\right) = \frac{1}{2}\left(f(s) + g(s) - g(s) + f(s)\right) = \frac{1}{2}(2f(s)) = f(s).$$
Thus, both sides evaluate to $f(s)$.

**Case 2:** $f(s) > g(s)$
In this case, $\min\{f(s), g(s)\} = g(s)$.
Since $f(s) > g(s)$, we have $f(s) - g(s) > 0$, which implies $|f(s) - g(s)| = f(s) - g(s)$.
Substituting this into the right hand side expression, we get:
$$\frac{1}{2}\left(f(s) + g(s) - (f(s) - g(s))\right) = \frac{1}{2}\left(f(s) + g(s) - f(s) + g(s)\right) = \frac{1}{2}(2g(s)) = g(s).$$
Thus, both sides evaluate to $g(s)$.

In both cases, we have shown that for all $s \in S$,
$$(f \wedge g)(s) = \frac{1}{2}\left(f(s) + g(s) - |f(s) - g(s)|\right).$$
Since the functions agree at every point in their domain, they are equal.
Therefore, $f \wedge g = \frac{1}{2}(f + g - |f - g|)$. $\blacksquare$
